brief: Distribution before product — 6 founders who built an audience before writing a line of code.

slots.subtitle: Six founders who sold nothing yet earned everything by showing up before shipping a single feature.
slots.preview1: How Sahil grew to 100K before Gumroad's rewrite
slots.preview2: Pieter Levels shipped audience, then code
slots.preview3: Jack Butcher drew his way to millions

slots.title: Followers first,
slots.subtitle: Sahil built a design following years before Gumroad's first commit.
slots.insight1Body: He posted designs on Tumblr daily, attracting his first 10,000 readers.
slots.insight2Body: Announced the idea before writing code; 200 creators paid in 48 hours.
slots.insight3Body: Pre-sold to an audience that already trusted his taste and speed.
slots.pullQuote: The audience is the moat; the product is just the receipt.

slots.title: Build in public,
slots.subtitle: Pieter's 12-startup blog built the distribution engine for Nomad List.
slots.insight1Body: Blogged every failure, turning curiosity into a mailing list of 50,000.
slots.insight2Body: Shared mockups and data; followers decided which project he should finish.
slots.insight3Body: When Nomad List launched, the audience paid before the homepage loaded.
slots.pullQuote: If nobody is watching, nobody is buying. Attention is the first feature.

slots.title: Teach the craft,
slots.subtitle: Nathan wrote two books and a blog before opening ConvertKit's repository.
slots.insight1Body: Self-published design guides that earned trust and 10,000 email subscribers.
slots.insight2Body: Realized readers struggled with email tools; the product idea surfaced from replies.
slots.insight3Body: Launched ConvertKit to an existing list of authors who already knew his voice.
slots.pullQuote: Your readers are your first users; treat every chapter as a prototype.

slots.title: Course first,
slots.subtitle: Adam taught Laravel and UI design before Tailwind CSS changed the web.
slots.insight1Body: Screencasts on CSS architecture revealed a demand for better tooling.
slots.insight2Body: Guest posts and podcast tours seeded his framework idea to 100,000 developers.
slots.insight3Body: Released a preview to his course list; GitHub stars funded the first version.
slots.pullQuote: Students asked for the tool; I just had to write the documentation first.

slots.title: Visualize value,
slots.subtitle: Jack grew a Twitter audience to 200K before Visualize Value had a store.
slots.insight1Body: Created philosophical visuals that spread faster than any product announcement could.
slots.insight2Body: Built a recognizable style so followers associated clarity with his brand instantly.
slots.insight3Body: Turned popular tweets into templates, courses, and prints his audience already wanted.
slots.pullQuote: The feed is the factory; every like is a focus group for your next SKU.

slots.title: Audience as
slots.subtitle: Justin built a solo empire by treating LinkedIn as his primary product for years.
slots.insight1Body: Wrote 1,000 LinkedIn posts before selling a single course or template.
slots.insight2Body: Turned comment sections into focus groups that shaped his digital product suite.
slots.insight3Body: Built a content flywheel so new followers converted to buyers while he slept.
slots.pullQuote: Your distribution network is worth more than your codebase. Guard it fiercely.

slots.ctaBody: The best code is worthless without eyes on it. Build your audience before your stack.
